- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction.  
- Model consistently underestimates in early periods of a 30-day forecast (e.g., days 1–5), especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; add 0.5–1.5% to early forecast values.  
- If sentiment shows a clear reversal (e.g., from positive to negative or vice versa), model lags in adjusting; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to align with sentiment shift.  
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if model is above 70–75% of recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecasts by averaging 3–5 prior values unless sentiment is clearly trending.
